name: or-motion-scene
description: Author, validate and materialise a deterministic MotionScene in the open OR project through mcp__or__motion_insert_scene — code-to-illustration, animated titles, diagrams and reusable scene JSON. Use when the user asks for an illustration, motion graphic or scene from code. Do NOT use for ordinary edits (or-timeline-edit) or for changing OR's own MotionScene implementation.

# Motion scene

Workspace guide: `docs/motion-scenes.md`.

## Procedure

1. Decide the input: a source file (code illustration) or an authored
   `.ormotion.json` (title, diagram, reusable scene).
2. For a scene, start from `node tools/motion-scaffold.mjs --name "Title"
   --out scenes/title.ormotion.json`, then edit nodes, text, colours, sizes and
   keyframes.
3. Validate with `tools/or motion validate --file scenes/title.ormotion.json
   --json` when the CLI exists. Fix every diagnostic; do not render a scene that
   fails validation.
4. Place it with `mcp__or__motion_insert_scene {scene_path}` or `{source_path}`.
   Materialisation encodes every frame: wait for the result and never run two at
   once.
5. Verify the clip appears with `timeline_overview`, then `save` unless the user
   asked to review first.

## Rules

- The scene is declarative and bounded: no expressions, scripts, network assets
  or provider calls. Refer to assets by scene-local or project-relative path.
- Text is literal; changing the title means changing the `text` field.
- A re-render never replaces the existing clip. Insert the new render and remove
  the old clip only when the user asks.
- Keep scenes short; a long scene is slow to encode and hard to revise.
- A reusable asset is catalogued and instantiated through
  `tools/or motion asset ...` (a library folder the user names); there is no
  asset tool on `mcp__or__` yet.

## Report

State the scene file, its duration and canvas, the track and time the clip was
inserted at, and whether the project was saved.

name: or-project-safety
description: Protect the open OR project while editing — check revision and dirty state, save explicitly, undo or redo canonical history, handle refused commands and report honestly. Use before any save, undo or recovery decision, or when a project tool call fails unexpectedly. Do NOT use for designing OR's history or command model.
---

# Project safety

Workspace guide: `docs/project-safety.md`.

## Procedure

1. Before changing anything, read `mcp__or__project_status`.
2. After the requested change, read the affected state (`timeline_overview` or
   `media_list`).
3. Save once with `mcp__or__save` unless the user asked to review first.
4. If the user wants a change undone, use `mcp__or__undo` and say how many edits
   it covered. Never close, shut down or reset the project.

## Rules

- Never write a `.orproj` file or any project path directly.
- A revision conflict or refused edit: re-read, retry once with real values, then
  stop and report.
- `dirty` is evidence. If an edit succeeded but the project is not dirty, report
  the inconsistency instead of claiming success.
- Do not invent tool success. Every claim names the tool and the state you read.

# Timeline edit

Workspace guide: `docs/timeline-editing.md`.

## Procedure

1. `mcp__or__project_status` — confirm the project and read the revision.
2. `mcp__or__timeline_overview` — read rates, tracks, clips and markers. Use only
   ids and times from this result.
3. Choose the smallest command. If the target track does not exist, create it
   with `add_track`; text and caption clips need a text or caption track.
4. Call the tool with exact `NUM/DEN` or decimal times.
5. `timeline_overview` again when placement matters, then `mcp__or__save` unless
   the user asked to review first.

## Rules

- One requested change per turn; do not bundle unrequested edits.
- Never invent ids or times from the prompt. The panel context names the current
  clip and playhead only when they exist.
- `insert` moves later clips right; `overwrite` clears the range. Say which one
  you used.
- A refused edit is information: re-read, retry once with valid values, then
  report.

## Report

Name the track, the clip and the exact time that changed, and whether the project
was saved.

# OR Agent Workspace

This is the operating workspace the Opencut Reinforced assistant uses by default.
It is not the OR source checkout. The open project is recorded in `project.json`,
and the `mcp__or__*` tools are the only way to read or change that project.

## Rule

Read the smallest entry that answers the current task. Do not preload the guides:
each line below names the situation that makes it the right thing to read.

## Routing

### Guides

- **Timeline editing** — tracks, clips, markers and sequence commands with exact times.
  When: the user asks to add, move, trim, split, delete, reorder, re-time or mark something on the timeline.
  Path: `docs/timeline-editing.md`
- **Media and import** — media ids, importing, paging and source relinking.
  When: the task needs a file in the library before it can be placed, or needs an existing media id.
  Path: `docs/media-and-import.md`
- **Motion scenes** — code-to-video scenes, `.ormotion.json`, validation and materialisation.
  When: the user asks for an illustration, motion graphic, animated title or scene from code.
  Path: `docs/motion-scenes.md`
- **Project safety** — revisions, save, undo/redo and refused operations.
  When: deciding whether to save, undoing a change, or recovering from a failed tool call.
  Path: `docs/project-safety.md`
- **Troubleshooting** — missing tools, no open project, slow or failed renders.
  When: a tool call fails and the error is not self-explanatory.
  Path: `docs/troubleshooting.md`

### Skills

The session catalog carries these. Load one only when its task matches.

- `or-timeline-edit` — orient, act, verify and save one timeline change.
- `or-motion-scene` — author, validate and materialise a deterministic scene.
- `or-project-safety` — protect revisions and report edits honestly.

### Tools

- `tools/or` — the OR CLI bound to the app build. Use it for
  `motion validate`, `inspect`, `from-code` and `render` when a scene must be
  checked without starting a materialisation. If it is missing, see
  `docs/troubleshooting.md`.
- `tools/motion-scaffold.mjs` — writes a valid V1 `.ormotion.json` skeleton:
  `node tools/motion-scaffold.mjs --name "Title" --out scenes/title.ormotion.json`.
- `tools/or motion asset ...` — validate, save, list or instantiate a reusable
  motion asset against a library folder the user names. The app does not expose
  an asset MCP tool yet; prefer `mcp__or__*` for anything on the timeline.

## Working files

- `scenes/` — scene sources you author. `mcp__or__motion_insert_scene` reads them.
- `work/` — scratch files, notes and copies. Nothing here is project state.
- `project.json`, `or-cli.json` and `tools/or` are written by the app; leave them alone.

## Bounds

- Never edit a `.orproj` file, the project directory, or any path listed in `project.json`.
- Project mutations happen only through `mcp__or__*` calls; imports read local files,
  so a file you copy into `work/` can be imported from there.
- Make one requested change at a time, confirm it with `timeline_overview`, then save
  unless the user asked to review first.

# Media and import

Scope: getting a file into the project library and finding the id that the
timeline commands take. The library is project state; importing is a project
mutation and is saved like any other edit.

## Order of operations

1. `mcp__or__media_list` — check whether the file is already imported. The list
   is paged: pass `offset` while `has_more` is true.
2. `mcp__or__add_media {source_path}` — import an **absolute** path. The result
   carries the new `media_id` and its metadata.
3. Place it with `insert_clip` (see [timeline-editing.md](timeline-editing.md)).
4. `mcp__or__save` after the edit, unless the user asked to review first.

## What can be imported

- Video, audio and image files that the app's FFmpeg build decodes.
- A file must exist and be readable when `add_media` runs; the library records a
  source path, not a copy.
- Importing the same path twice is allowed; use the id the new call returns.

## Paths

- `source_path` must be absolute. The workspace sits outside the project, so a
  path relative to the project is not automatically correct.
- Files the agent downloaded or wrote live under `work/`; copy or keep them there
  and pass that absolute path.
- Do not move or delete a source file after importing it; the project would need
  a relink, and no MCP tool performs relink yet.

## Reading metadata

`media_list` returns ids, source paths and duration metadata. Use the returned
duration when you need a clip length; do not round it into a different time base.
`project_status` reports the project revision and dirty state.

# Motion scenes

Scope: turning code or a declarative `.ormotion.json` scene into an ordinary,
editable video clip through the app's deterministic MotionScene renderer. No
provider or network call happens here.

## Two inputs

| Input | Use |
|---|---|
| A source file | `mcp__or__motion_insert_scene {source_path: "work/sample.rs"}` turns the code into a highlighted illustration. |
| A scene file | `mcp__or__motion_insert_scene {scene_path: "scenes/title.ormotion.json"}` renders an authored scene. |

Pass exactly one of `source_path` and `scene_path`. The call materialises video
frames through the app, imports the result and inserts an ordinary clip. It is
slow because every frame is encoded; do not start a second render while one is
running and do not retry after a timeout without checking the timeline.

Useful optional arguments: `title`, `at`, `track_id`, `width`, `height`,
`frame_rate` (`30/1`), `output_path`.

## Authoring a scene

Start from the scaffold, then edit the JSON:

```sh
node tools/motion-scaffold.mjs --name "Title" --out scenes/title.ormotion.json
```

Validate before rendering:

```sh
tools/or motion validate --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --json
```

`tools/or motion inspect` summarises nodes and animation counts;
`tools/or motion render` rasterises one frame to a PNG when a still is enough.
`tools/or motion from-code` writes a scene from a source file without
materialising it, so the agent can adjust the generated scene first.

## Envelope

```json
{
  "format": "opencut-reinforced-motion-scene",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "scene_id": "<UUIDv4>",
  "name": "...",
  "duration": {"numerator": 4, "denominator": 1},
  "canvas": {"width": 1920, "height": 1080},
  "assets": [],
  "nodes": [],
  "animations": []
}
```

Node kinds: `group`, `text`, `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `arrow`, `image`.

- Text needs `text`; optional `position`, `font_size`, `fill`, `spans`
  (byte-offset highlight runs).
- Rectangle and ellipse need `size`; optional `position`, `fill`, `stroke`,
  `stroke_width`, `rotation_degrees`, `opacity`.
- Image needs `asset_id`; group needs `children`.
- Colours are typed `{red, green, blue, alpha}` with 0–255 channels. There is no
  CSS string and no expression language.
- Animated properties are `translation_x`, `translation_y`, `scale`, `rotation`,
  `opacity`, `width`, `height`. Keyframes are ascending, inside `[0, duration]`,
  and each node animates a property once. Easings: `linear`, `ease_in`,
  `ease_out`, `ease_in_out`.

To change the title, a colour or a size, edit the node's fields and re-materialise.
The materialised clip already on the timeline is an ordinary video clip; re-running
the scene never silently replaces it — insert the new render and delete the old
clip only if the user asks.

## Reusable assets

A motion asset (`.ormotionasset.json`, ADR 0010) wraps a scene template or a
fragment with typed parameters for text, colour, size, opacity and rotation.
The app has no asset MCP tool yet; when the user names a library folder, use the
CLI:

```sh
tools/or motion asset list --library PATH --json
tools/or motion asset save --library PATH --file scenes/title.ormotionasset.json --json
tools/or motion asset instantiate --library PATH --id ASSET_ID \
  --values '{"title":"Hello"}' --output scenes/instantiated.ormotion.json
```

`--values` is a JSON object keyed by parameter id. Saving recomputes the category
from tags and the name unless it is explicit; pass `--category` to override it.
An instantiated scene is an ordinary `.ormotion.json` you can validate and then
pass to `mcp__or__motion_insert_scene`.

## Bounds

A scene file is at most 4 MiB, 4096 nodes, groups nested 16 deep, 4096
animations, 4096 keyframes per animation, 64 KiB per text node. Asset paths must
be scene-local or project-relative; remote URLs are refused. Keep scenes short:
a ten-second 30 fps scene is 300 encoded frames.

# Project safety

Scope: how to change a live project without losing work. Rust owns the project,
its revision and its history; every `mcp__or__*` mutation goes through the same
validated command path as the editor.

## The one rule

Never edit a `.orproj` file or anything inside the project directory directly.
The running app holds the authoritative document; a direct edit is invisible to
it and will be overwritten or rejected. Use the MCP tools.

## Reading state

`mcp__or__project_status` returns the project name, file, revision and dirty
state. `timeline_overview` and `media_list` are reads: they never mutate.

Edits are live in the app as soon as the tool succeeds, but they are unsaved
until `save` runs. `dirty: false` after an edit means something is wrong; report
it instead of claiming success.

## Save and history

- Call `mcp__or__save` once after finishing the requested change, unless the user
  asked to review first.
- `mcp__or__undo` and `mcp__or__redo` are the canonical history. They undo one
  project edit, not one conversation turn; tell the user how many steps you
  undid.
- Never call any project, session or recovery shutdown. Closing the app is the
  user's action.

## Refused operations

A refused command is a real answer, not a transient error:

- A time outside the sequence or a trim that inverts a clip: re-read the
  timeline and choose a valid time.
- A revision conflict: re-read `project_status`, then repeat the edit once.
- A duplicate id or a missing media id: re-read ids and retry with real values.

Do not loop on the same failing call. After two identical failures, stop and
report the tool, its error and the next concrete step.

## Reporting

Say what changed: track, clip, exact time. Say what was saved. Do not claim a
change that no tool confirmed; a timeline read after the edit is the minimum
evidence.

# Timeline editing

Scope: the exact-time timeline commands the assistant may call. Project state is
Rust-owned; read [project-safety.md](project-safety.md) before saving or undoing.

## Order of operations

1. `mcp__or__project_status` — confirm a project is open and read its revision.
2. `mcp__or__timeline_overview` — read the sequence rate, tracks, clips and markers.
3. Use only the ids and times that call returned. Never invent a `clip_id`,
   `track_id` or media id.
4. Make the smallest command the request needs.
5. `mcp__or__timeline_overview` again when the placement matters.
6. `mcp__or__save` unless the user asked to review first.

## Time form

- Times are exact `NUM/DEN` seconds or decimal seconds (`"2.5"`, `"1.25s"`).
- Durations default to the media's full length when omitted.
- A clip's `at` is its timeline start; `source_start` addresses the media in-point.
- Do not guess a position from the prompt. The panel sends the selected clip and
  playhead as context when they exist; otherwise ask or append after the last clip.

## Commands

| Tool | Use |
|---|---|
| `add_track` | Add an empty `video`, `audio`, `text` or `caption` track. |
| `insert_clip` | Place imported media at an exact time. Default mode `insert` moves later clips right; `overwrite` clears the range. |
| `insert_text` | Add a `text` or `caption` clip on a text/caption track. |
| `move_clip` | Move a clip in time, optionally to another track. |
| `trim_clip` | Trim the `start` or `end` edge to an exact timeline time. |
| `split_clip` | Split a clip at a time; the right-hand part starts there. |
| `delete_clip` | Delete a clip; `ripple: true` closes the gap on that track. |
| `set_frame_rate` | Set the sequence rate from `NUM/DEN`. |
| `add_marker` | Add a labelled marker at a time. |

## Track and clip rules

- Visual tracks (`video`, `text`, `caption`) carry visual clips; `audio` tracks
  carry audio clips. A text clip on a video track is refused.
- `insert_text` requires a text or caption track; create one with `add_track` if
  the timeline has none.
- Clips cannot overlap on one track. `insert` makes room, `overwrite` replaces it.
- Track order on screen is the order `timeline_overview` returns.

## Examples

Append a five-second clip to the end of the first video track:

1. `media_list` → choose `media_id`; `timeline_overview` → read the track's last
   clip end.
2. `insert_clip {track_id, media_id, at: "<end>"}` (duration defaults to full).
3. `timeline_overview`, then `save`.

Trim the selected clip to end at 4 s:

1. The panel context names the clip and its track.
2. `trim_clip {clip_id, edge: "end", at: "4"}`.
3. Verify the duration is positive; a trim that would invert the clip is refused.

# Troubleshooting

Scope: the failures the assistant can meet inside this workspace, and the next
concrete step for each. Report the cause, never a guessed success.

## No tools are available

If the session has no `mcp__or__*` tools, the `or` MCP server did not attach.
The assistant panel shows a setup error for a missing harness or CLI. Stop
editing and tell the user to reconnect the assistant; do not try to reach the
project another way.

## `project_status` fails

The app has no open project, or the session pointer is stale. Ask the user to
open or create a project in OR, then retry once. `workspace` does not have to be
the project directory; the pointer carries the real project path.

## `tools/or` is missing or not executable

The app writes `tools/or` when it connects to the app build. If it is absent,
run the scene check another way: `mcp__or__motion_insert_scene` validates the
scene during materialisation and returns the diagnostic codes. Do not write your
own renderer.

## Materialisation is slow

`motion_insert_scene` encodes every frame with the app's encoder. A short scene
still takes seconds to minutes. Wait for the tool result; do not start a second
render and do not retry after a timeout without checking whether the clip
appeared. If a render fails, read the returned code, fix the scene, and retry
once.

## Scene validation codes

Common codes and their fix:

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `MOTION_INVALID_SCENE_ID` | `scene_id` must be a fresh UUIDv4. |
| `MOTION_INVALID_DURATION` | `duration` must be greater than zero. |
| `MOTION_MISSING_TEXT` / `MOTION_MISSING_SIZE` | Add the field the node kind requires. |
| `MOTION_KEYFRAMES_UNSORTED` / `MOTION_KEYFRAME_OUT_OF_RANGE` | Sort keyframes and keep them inside the duration. |
| `MOTION_ANIMATION_UNKNOWN_NODE` | The `node_id` must exist in `nodes`. |
| `MOTION_REMOTE_ASSET_REFUSED` | Use a scene-local or project-relative asset path. |

## A tool call is refused

See [project-safety.md](project-safety.md). Re-read state, retry once with real
ids and times, then report the refusal if it repeats.

# Workspace tools

Scope: the local commands this workspace exposes. They complement the
`mcp__or__*` tools; they never mutate the project.

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `tools/or <args>` | The OR CLI bound to the running app build. `motion validate`, `inspect`, `from-code`, `render`, `media probe`. App-generated; if missing, see `docs/troubleshooting.md`. |
| `node tools/motion-scaffold.mjs` | Write a valid V1 `.ormotion.json` skeleton into `scenes/`. |
| `tools/or motion asset ...` | Validate, save, list or instantiate a reusable motion asset against a library folder. |

## Examples

```sh
tools/or motion validate --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --json
tools/or motion inspect --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --json
tools/or motion from-code --source work/sample.rs --output scenes/sample.ormotion.json
tools/or motion render --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --at 1/2 --output work/title.png
tools/or motion asset list --library work/motion-library --json
```

`motion materialize` needs a live app, so prefer `mcp__or__motion_insert_scene`
for insertion. Use the CLI verbs above only to check or preview a scene first.

## Bounds

- `tools/or` is written by the app on connect; editing it is pointless.
- Scaffold and CLI write only the files you name; nothing is project state.
